title: Analysis of microvasculature in patients with virus associated anterior uveitis using OCTA
summary:
Intraocular inflammation or uveitis is a common cause of vision problems worldwide. They occur in all age groups, with an accumulation between the ages of 20 and 40. The recurrence of these inflammations is about 30%. In about 50% of affected patients, an underlying disease or associated characteristics can be identified.
Inflammation of the uvea is classified into anterior, posterior, intermediate or panuveitis, depending on the structures affected. 
In anterior uveitis, various viruses are often the trigger and are then often characterized by recurring attacks of usually one-sided increased intraocular pressure. The exact causes are not yet fully understood, but infection with viruses seems to play an important role.
So far, no information has been carried out on changes in the function of the vessels of the retina. A new examination method is now to be used to investigate whether there are differences in the vascular density of the individual retinal layers between the eye, which is affected by the virus-associated inflammation, and the other, healthy eye.

interventions.name: Patients with anterior virus-associated uveitis are examined by optical coherence tomography-angiography. The eye affected by anterior uveitis is compared to the contralateral, healthy eye.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
confirmed diagnosis of virus-positive AU
Exclusion criteria:
- refractive errors of the sphere or the cylinder more than -3.50 diopters
-  a history of other retinal diseases (diabetic retinopathy, age-related macular degeneration).
